Considering such conduct from insurance company and taking note of the fact that insurance Dar-Najma vs Punit Kumar on 10 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107466864/

Only point of difference was whether the minimum wages to be invoked for calculating the notional income of the petitioner/deceased should be one which is applicable in State of UP or in State of NCT of Delhi.
This Tribunal proceeds to decide the question of amount of compensation as there is otherwise no dispute or defence raised on behalf of respondents.

10. The question of rash and negligent driving in a matter arises u/s 166/140 of M.V. Act can be taken up by noting down that police in this case regarding the accident in question had registered FIR No.658/2022 at PS Seema Puri wherein police filed the charge sheet and prosecuted driver of the offending vehicle namely respondent no.1 Punit Kumar.
Nothing except the bald denial of accident, came in the pleadings of respondent no.1 and 2.
Therefore this aspect is taken to be proved on the record by the factum of filing of DAR itself and not raising any other issue.
MACT No.167/2023 (in death case) Quantum of compensation 11.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for the MACT Nos.167/2023 & 168/2023 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER Page 5 MALIK Date:
2024.05.10 16:18:16 +0530 physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12.
The present case pertains to the death of deceased Sahvej.

In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.

sentences.text: Further, the guidelines have been reiterated by the Constitution Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case titled as National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. Decided on 31.10.2017, laying down the general principles for computation of compensation in death cases.

"18.

Basically only three facts need to be established by the claimants for assessing compensation in the case of death:
(a) age of the deceased;
(b) income of the deceased; and (c) the number of dependents.

To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

5
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."

Therefore, in view of the aforesaid judgment, it is essential to take into consideration the following parameters:-

PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
Age and assessment of income of deceased 14.
As per the contents of the DAR deceased Sahvej was 18 years of age at the time of accident.
Deceased was doing a private work.

As per the facts injured Sohil along with his friend/deceased Sahvej went on motorcycle for bringing milk for the niece of the injured Sohil Khan when accident took place in the area of Seema Puri, Delhi.
In the absence of any documentary evidence regarding the income, this Tribunal has to decide the notional income.

Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav and others 2021 (2) TNMAC 498 (SC), in para 10 has held "in the absence of any documentary evidence on record, some amount of guess work is required to be done.

Merely because claimant has unable to produce documentary evidence to show the monthly income of Shiv Pal, same does not justify adaption lowest tier of minimum wages, while computing the income....."
15. Thus in the present case, minimum wages is to be invoked for assessing the notional income of the deceased.
Question for consideration is whether minimum wages of State of UP should be taken or minimum wages of Delhi should be taken.

16. Generally there is hardly any dispute on the question of taking minimum wages into consideration for deciding the notional income of deceased/injured in a motor accident claim petition, in Delhi as generally accident take place in Delhi and petitioner is also resident of Delhi.

sentences.text: 18. The aspect of minimum wages to be invoked has generally been left for Tribunal to examine in the peculiar facts and circumstances of each case with broad preposition of law in mind that the Tribunal has to decide the amount of compensation to be just and fair.

In this context it is useful to give observation of Punjab & Haryana High Court in the matter of United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
vs. Sunil and ors.

"the income provided in Minimum Wages Act revised from time to time, can be basic criteria or guideline to assess the income of deceased or injured as the case may be.
The facts and circumstances of each case has to be evaluated.
No restriction can be imposed in assessing the income of deceased or the injured in order to assess just and fair compensation for the dependents."
19. In the facts of the present case accident has occurred in Delhi.

The circumstances in which accident has occurred and overall circumstances, to the mind of this Tribunal weigh more towards assessing the income of deceased on the basis of minimum wages applicable in Delhi at the time of accident.

The fact that deceased was resident of UP though MACT Nos.167/2023 & 168/2023 by SHAILENDER Page 9 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.10 16:18:47 +0530 has relevant fact but it is to be seen that it is established residence, only then that aspect can be taken into consideration.

Therefore this Tribunal is of considered view that ends of justice would meet by taking into consideration the minimum wages of unskilled worker Delhi at the time of accident which is Rs.16,506/- per month.

20.

An appropriate multiplier has to be determined for computation of compensation.
The judgment titled as Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121 is relevant to consider the multiplier.

Future Prospects:
22.
This issue was considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in MACT Nos.167/2023 & 168/2023 by SHAILENDER Page 10 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK

Relevant parts of the judgment are reproduced here as under:
"(iii) While determining the income, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The addition should be 30%, if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.

(iv) In case, the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40%
of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component."

23. Since on the day of accident deceased was aged around 18 years, in view of said fact this Tribunal finds that 40% of the income of deceased (aged below 40 years) has to be considered towards future prospects.

NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
26.

In case of Pranay Sethi (Supra), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/-
respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.

Therefore, a compensation of Rs.48,000/-,
18,000/- and Rs.18,000/- respectively on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is required to be granted.

Further, in view of recent decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors., Civil Appeal no. 2705 of 2020, decided on 30.06.2020, loss of consortium has to be fixed for each of the LRs.

Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
33.
In the present case as is evident from the DAR and documents annexed with it including MLC of petitioner/injured, he has suffered injuries on his forehead, cheek, nose and right knee.
Due to such injuries it is presumed that petitioner must have taken special diet for early healing of his wounds and must have spent money on going to hospital(s).
Thus this Tribunal assesses the amount of compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head of special diet and Rs.10,000/- under the head of conveyance charges.

Attendant Charges:
34.
So far as attendant charges are concerned, this Tribunal has already assessed the period of loss of income of petitioner due to accidental injuries to be of two months.

Therefore on the same analogy this Tribunal is of the view that for the said period when the petitioner had taken treatment and not able to do any work, it would be in the fitness of things to grant him attendant charges @
Rs.20,000/-.
Thus, compensation of Rs.20,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head..

Pain & Sufferings:
35.

In view of the pronouncement of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision:

nose and injury on right knee due to accidental injuries.
In such circumstance this Tribunal finds that the petitioner has suffered pain and suffering due to multiple injuries received in the accident in question.

It is however very difficult to quantify the pain and suffering of anyone received injuries in an accident, in the circumstances of the present case having regard to medical difficulties faced by petitioner, age, this Tribunal finds that petitioner is certainly entitled for sum of Rs.50,000/- on account of pain and suffering.

36.

It cannot be ignored that with said injuries, petitioner is bound to face some difficulties throughout his life and will not be able to enjoy the amenities of life to the fullest.
In view of this, the petitioner is granted a compensation of Rs.15,000/- under this head.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
In death cases, the guidelines for computation of compensation have been laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and Others v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr. (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121.
To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balanc expired e which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Step-2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)
The annual contribution to the family(multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.
The funeral expenses, cost of transportation of the body (if incurred) and the cost of any medical treatment of the deceased before death (if incurred) should also be added."
Deceased was doing a private work.
18. The aspect of minimum wages to be invoked has generally been left for Tribunal to examine in the peculiar facts and circumstances of each case with broad preposition of law in mind that the Tribunal has to decide the amount of compensation to be just and fair.
The circumstances in which accident has occurred and overall circumstances, to the mind of this Tribunal weigh more towards assessing the income of deceased on the basis of minimum wages applicable in Delhi at the time of accident.
The fact that deceased was resident of UP though MACT Nos.167/2023 & 168/2023 by SHAILENDER Page 9 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.10 16:18:47 +0530 has relevant fact but it is to be seen that it is established residence, only then that aspect can be taken into consideration.
